source: Minchat Shai on Gen 1:14 (Pesikta; Yerushalmi Taanit; Kitzur Baal HaTurim)
claim_en: meorot ('luminaries') in the command is written DOUBLY LEAN — no vav at all, the skeleton of meera ('curse'): the Pesikta's 'only the sun's orb was created to give light' and the Yerushalmi's Wednesday fast over the children's croup both hang on this spelling; bare form once in the Torah.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 1:15 quoting the Ramah
claim_en: The Ramah's census: 'meorot — TWO doubly lean in the language, sign: yehi meorot (1:14) and et shene ha-meorot (1:16)' — the second station, with the article, also once in the Torah.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 1:14 (the Zohar's list)
claim_en: le-otot ('for signs') is lean-of-lean too — no vav in either slot — and this doubly-lean form stands once in the Torah.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 1:15 (handwritten Masorah; the Hilleli codex; the Ramah)
claim_en: li-meorot ('for luminaries', 1:15) is FULL in the first vav and lean in the second — the handwritten Masorah note, the manuscripts, the early print, and the spelling list MS copied from the 900-year-old Hilleli codex, all matched in-stream.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 1:16 quoting the Ramah (against the handwritten Masorah's 'unique-and-lean')
claim_en: ha-maor ('the luminary'): the Ramah rules it FULL, 'and every maor-language in the Torah likewise full except one' — SNAPSHOT writes the full form at all seven article-stations: the great and the small light here, the lamp-verses of the Tabernacle, and the lamp-charge of Numbers.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 1:16 quoting the Ramah
claim_en: The Ramah's ONE exception, his own sign: shemen la-maor ('oil for the light'), the FIRST of the Terumah portion — the single lean maor-word in the Torah, exactly where he said it stands.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 1:16 quoting the Ramah
claim_en: The rule's other half: every remaining la-maor ('for the light') is FULL — four stations (the eternal-lamp commands of Exodus and Leviticus, the anointing-oil list, the freewill gifts).

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 1:18 (Et Sofer; Meiri's Kiryat Sefer)
claim_en: u-la-havdil ('and to divide', 1:18): Et Sofer and the Meiri rule the vav carries a geiya (the small stress-stroke) — SNAPSHOT writes it in-stream.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 1:18 (the books divided)
claim_en: The same word's lamed: MS records the books DIVIDED — plain sheva (the silent half-vowel) in some, sheva-patach (the hataf half-vowel) in others. SNAPSHOT writes the HATAF under the lamed while ALSO carrying Et Sofer's geiya — a mixed station joining both camps' marks: the half-vowel law's lamed again, split-attested.
MS closes: 'the word's accent is zaqef qatan (the small two-dot pause)' — in-stream.
